title: Whisk Rush
hook: Whisk one shared batch and race to turn it into layered drinks before either the foam or the customers lose patience.
audience: Cooking and time-management players who enjoy physical preparation and recovering a difficult service.
core_loop: Choose a small menu; prepare shared batches; pour and serve competing orders; trade preparation against freshness; buy one equipment improvement; retry short shifts for a better service.
score_notes: See management-trends.md for independent source periods, scope breakdown and counterevidence.

inspiration.topic: Speciality drinks, including matcha and hojicha
inspiration.connection: Ingredients and satisfying preparation come from the trend; service timing, shared resources and recovery provide the enduring game.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: Preparation, triage, dexterity and equipment tradeoffs can work with any drink menu.
inspiration.current_timing: Historical source growth or current expansion is recorded separately; September search slope and future peak are unverified.

commercial_hypothesis.condition: Genre/price evidence and a worthwhile finished experience within the work budget are both required. These are test prices, not selected prices or sales forecasts.

prototype_envelope.scope: One-day prototype with two recipes, two cup slots and a shared bowl. With five available service-game players, continue if four serve independently, three make a deliberate freshness-versus-preparation tradeoff and three choose another shift. Check the whisk action after twenty drinks. Hold if repeated motion is an obstruction or speed-clicking solves all orders.

production_envelope.scope: One fixed 2D counter, four recipes, three short shifts plus seeded score replay, two cup slots initially and three equipment choices, save/settings/tutorial and package.
production_envelope.note: Includes prototype, original modest art/audio, finite content, controls/settings/save, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Calendar onboarding/review, recruitment and unforeseen rework are separate. Estimate is not demonstrated.

cash_assumptions.note: Existing tools assumed. No purchases or cash allocation. Steam fee and optional assets remain separate planning inputs in the run.

support_estimate: Allow 1–2 owner hours for launch-month triage/review, plus agent fixes as needed; actual burden unknown.

evidence.claim: Updated August 25, 2026: banana matcha latte +6,900% over five years with 1.3K monthly searches; exact endpoints and total geography unspecified. Not evidence of current acceleration.

November 13, 2025 Square US report: matcha orders +36.5% year over year in Q3 2025 versus +44.3% in Q2, indicating slower growth. Cohort details incomplete; neither PC game demand nor banana-specific data.
Boba Simulator: USD 3.99 regular / 3.11 current, 315 consistently filtered reviews. Lower-price but broader idle management competition.
Coffee Caravan: USD 11.99 regular/current, 1,395 reviews. Close service competitor above the owner's price ceiling; useful for overlap and quality, not in-band price proof.
Boba Cafe Simulator: USD 15.99 regular / 14.39 current, 1,155 reviews. Recent larger competitor, above ceiling.

Developer postmortem reuploaded July 11, 2025, originally around June 2024: Minami Lane sold 50,000 copies in its first month, regular price USD 4.99, made in less than six months by a programmer and artist with commissioned audio. Adjacent management sales evidence, not proof of our development time.

risks: Coffee Caravan already includes matcha; the ingredient is not a mechanical gap.
Close hands-on competitors offer more systems; USD 9.99 is not yet justified.
A repeated whisk gesture could become tiring.
The independent Square order data ends in 2025 and shows deceleration.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No own playable build, competitor hands-on test, measured organic conversion, target-player willingness to pay or validated production time. Current names are working titles without clearance.
next_test: One-day prototype with two recipes, two cup slots and a shared bowl. With five available service-game players, continue if four serve independently, three make a deliberate freshness-versus-preparation tradeoff and three choose another shift. Check the whisk action after twenty drinks. Hold if repeated motion is an obstruction or speed-clicking solves all orders.
decision_reason: Second recommended experiment for a clear service fantasy, trend-inspired materials and an established low-price management audience; the shared-batch decision must distinguish it.
